now.title: The Spectacular Spider-Man#10
now.text: Quentin Beck works on the Chameleon's scheme to frame Spider-Man.
now.on_a_card_about_b: The hero Mysterio haunts with tricks and decoys.
now.on_b_card_about_a: A master of illusions Peter never quite catches.

proposed.on_a_card_about_b: The hero Beck helps the Chameleon frame.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A Chameleon henchman who helps frame Peter.

changes.evidence: In Persona (#10) Beck is only the Chameleon's henchman, using effects to pass the Chameleon off as Spider-Man; Black Cat knocks him out and he is arrested. He first appears as Mysterio, and first leaves a robot decoy in his place, in Blueprints (#14). The #10 card lines ('haunts with tricks and decoys', 'never quite catches') tell the #14 decoy twist early and contradict his arrest at #10.

owner_calls.question: Stage 0 sits at #7 but its first event, Spider-Man saving Norman from the Vulture, happens in #1 (Survival of the Fittest), where Peter also meets Norman at the Osborn home. Should the pair start at #1?
options: Move stage 0 to The Spectacular Spider-Man#1 (kind friend or ally) with the Vulture rescue, and add a #7 enemy stage for the Green Goblin's debut
Keep stage 0 at #7 and drop the Vulture clause from its text (the card line can keep it as past)
Leave as is (recap of #1 inside the #7 stage)
owner_calls.evidence: #1: the Vulture snatches Norman from his balcony and drops him, and Spider-Man catches him (his first civilian rescue), then protects him again from the Vulture that night. #7: the Green Goblin debuts and tries to kill Spider-Man.

owner_calls.question: Stage 0 at #12 links Peter to Walter Hardy (Black Cat's father) as Uncle Ben's killer, and its card line names Walter. On screen the burglar is unnamed at #12; that he is Walter Hardy, Black Cat's father, is the reveal of #25 (Opening Night). Does showing this pair from #12 give away the #25 reveal?
options: Start the pair at #25 and fold the #12 flashback into the #25 text
Keep the #12 stage (the app hides or allows the identity at #12)
Keep #12 but have the cards avoid tying him to Black Cat
owner_calls.evidence: #12 (Intervention): in Peter's mindscape the origin replays; the burglar Peter let go kills Ben, and Peter catches him and spares him. #25 (Opening Night): Black Cat reveals she came to free her father, Walter Hardy, the Cat Burglar, and Walter Hardy was the man who killed Uncle Ben.
